exampleAnswers.title: Identifying an Orthogonal Fundamental Subspaces of a Matrix

question.text:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Col}(B)$ for every matrix $B?$

  1. $\text{Null}(B^T)$
  2. $\text{Col}(B^T)$
  3. $\text{Null}(B)$
question.explanation:
Recall that $\text{Col}(B)$ consists of all linear combinations of the columns of $B$, that is, the rows of $B^T.$

If a vector is orthogonal to every linear combination of the rows of $B^T,$ it must be orthogonal to each row of $B^T.$ But notice that when pre-multiplying a vector by $B^T,$ we actually multiply each row of $B^T$ by that vector. So, $\text{Col}(B)$ must be orthogonal to the left null space of $B,$ which is $\text{Null}(B^T).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I only."

Note: In general, the four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $B$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

example.title: Identifying an Orthogonal Fundamental Subspaces of a Matrix

question.text:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Null}(X^T Y^T)$ for all compatible matrices $X$ and $Y?$

  1. $\text{Null}(YX)$
  2. $\text{Col}(X^TY^T)$
  3. $\text{Col}(YX)$
question.explanation:
Recall that $\text{Null}(X^T Y^T)$ contains all vectors that, when pre-multiplied by $X^T Y^T,$ result in the zero-vector $\mathbf{0}.$

When pre-multiplying a vector by $X^T Y^T,$ we actually multiply each row of $X^T Y^T$ by that vector. So, $\text{Null}(X^T Y^T)$ must be orthogonal to the row space of $X^T Y^T,$ which is $\text{Col}((X^T Y^T)^T)=\text{Col}(YX).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "III only."

example.title: Identifying an Orthogonal Fundamental Subspaces of a Matrix

question.text:
Which of the following subspaces must be orthogonal to $\text{Null}(A+B)$ for all compatible matrices $A$ and $B?$

  1. $\text{Null}(A^T+B^T)$
  2. $\text{Col}(A^T+B^T)$
  3. $\text{Col}(A+B)$
question.explanation:
Recall that $\text{Null}(A+B)$ contains all vectors that, when pre-multiplied by $A+B,$ result in the zero-vector $\mathbf{0}.$

When pre-multiplying a vector by $A+B,$ we actually multiply each row of $A+B$ by that vector. So, $\text{Null}(A+B)$ must be orthogonal to the row space of $A+B,$ which is $\text{Col}((A+B)^T)=\text{Col}(A^T+B^T).$

Therefore, the correct answer is "II only."

Note: In general, the four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $A$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

exampleAnswers.title: Identifying the Images of the Four Fundamental Subspaces of the Matrix Under Its Action

question.text: Let $A$ and $B$ be $m \times n$ matrices. What is the image of $\mathbb{R}^m$ under the action of $A^T+B^T?$
question.explanation:
First, notice that $A^T+B^T$ is a $n \times m$ matrix.

Now, pre-multiplying a vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^m$ by $A^T+B^T$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $A^T+B^T{:}$

\[ \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} \vert & \vert & \cdots & \vert \\ (a^T+b^T)_1 & (a^T+b^T)_2 & \cdots & (a^T+b^T)_m \\ \vert & \vert & \cdots & \vert \end{bmatrix}}_{\large A^T+B^T} \cdot \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ \vdots \\ x_m \end{bmatrix}}_{\large \mathbf{x}} = x_1 \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ (a^T+b^T)_1 \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ (a^T+b^T)_2 \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} +\cdots+ x_m \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ (a^T+b^T)_m \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} \]

Therefore, the image of $\mathbb{R}^m$ under the action of $A^T+B^T$ must be $\text{Col}(A^T+B^T),$ the row space of $A+B.$

example.title: Identifying the Images of the Four Fundamental Subspaces of the Matrix Under Its Action

question.text: Let $A$ be a $4 \times 6$ matrix. What is the image of $\mathbb{R}^4$ under the action of $A^T?$
question.explanation:
First, notice that $A^T$ is a $6 \times 4$ matrix.

Pre-multiplying a vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^4$ by $A^T$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $A^T{:}$

\[ \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} \vert & \vert & \vert & \vert \\ a_1^T & a_2^T & a_3^T & a_4^T \\ \vert & \vert & \vert & \vert \end{bmatrix}}_{\large A^T} \cdot \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ x_2 \\ x_3 \\ x_4 \end{bmatrix}}_{\large \mathbf{x}} = x_1 \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ a_1^T \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ a_2^T \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} + x_3 \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ a_3^T \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} + x_4 \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ a_4^T \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} \]

Therefore, the image of $\mathbb{R}^4$ under the action of $A^T$ must be $\text{Col}(A^T),$ the row space of $A.$

example.title: Identifying the Images of the Four Fundamental Subspaces of the Matrix Under Its Action

question.text: Let $A$ be a $m \times n$ matrix. What is the image of $\mathbb{R}^n$ under the action of $A?$
question.explanation:
Pre-multiplying a vector $\mathbf{x} \in \mathbb{R}^n$ by $A$ gives a linear combination of the columns of $A{:}$

\[ \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} \vert & \vert & \cdots & \vert \\ a_1 & a_2 & \cdots & a_n \\ \vert & \vert & \cdots & \vert \end{bmatrix}}_{\large A} \cdot \underbrace{\begin{bmatrix} x_1 \\ \vdots \\ x_n \end{bmatrix}}_{\large \mathbf{x}} = x_1 \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ a_1 \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} + x_2 \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ a_2 \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} +\cdots+ x_n \begin{bmatrix} \vert \\ a_n \\ \vert \end{bmatrix} \]

Therefore, the image of $\mathbb{R}^n$ under the action of $A$ must be $\text{Col}(A),$ the column space of $A.$

example.title: Finding the Dimensions of the Four Fundamental Subspaces of a Matrix

question.explanation:
The four fundamental subspaces of a matrix $A$ can be schematically visualized, as shown below.

In our case, we are given that $m=3,$ $n=4,$ and $m-r=2.$

Substituting $m=3$ into $m-r=2,$ we can find the rank of $A{:}$

\[ (3) - r = 2 \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad r = 1 \]

Therefore, we obtain

\begin{align*} \text{dim}(\text{Col}(A)) &= r = 1. \end{align*}
